 B.K.Venkatesh Murthy
 S/o Krishnamurthy
 Aged about 40 years
 R/o Bommadigere village
 Kothagere hobli
 Kunigal Taluk
 Tumkur district

 (By Sri.Dayananda K.H. Adv.)

Prakash

15th cross, Opp: Union Bank of India Yelahanka new town Bangalore560064 owner of Hyundai Accent car Reg.No.KA05MB0234 (Exparte)

2. The New India Assurance company Ltd., Unity Building tower block 4th floor,JC road Bangalore 560002, Karnataka Policy No.67210031200200000289 valid from 752020 upto 652021 (By Sri.Muralidhar Negavar Adv) JUDGMENT

This is a petition filed u/s 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules claiming for compensation of Rs.15,00,000/
with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
2.

The petitioner's case in brief:
B.K. Venkatesh Murthy vs Prakash.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51317535/

1 That on 2622021 at around 3.50 p.m. when the petitioner was riding Honda activa two wheeler vehicle bearing No.A06HE6965 from Kunigal side towards JUDGMENT Bettadarangaswamy temple side, near Anjaneya swamy temple road,
driver of the Hundai Accent car bearing reg.No.KA05MB0234 came from Bettadarangaswamy temple side with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner, as a result of which he fell down and sustained injuries and took treatment in the hospital as inpatient and spent more amount towards medical expenses.

The petitioner further stated that at the time of accident he was aged 40 years and was doing agriculture and earning more than Rs.5 lakhs p.a. and along with archak work and jyothisha sasthra telling he was earning Rs.1000/ per day and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity and lost his income.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.15 lakhs from the respondents.
3. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and he placed exparte and respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel.
The second respondent filed written statement wherein contended that the alleged JUDGMENT accident took place solely due to negligence of the petitioner himself.

The petitioner has not approached this court with clean hands and a false complaint has been lodged against the insured vehicle after laps of 4 days of the accident twisting the facts illegally and high handedly and colluding with concerned persons in order to get compensation from this court.
The driver of the insured vehicle alleged to have involved in the alleged accident was not having valid and effective DL.
The petitioner was riding th motor cycle without wearing helmet and without following the traffic rules and regulations.
The alleged accident as required u/s 134 (c) of the MV act like wise the jurisdictional police have not informed to this respondent as per Section 158 (6) of the MV Act.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

4. From the above said pleadings three issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the JUDGMENT driver of the car bearing reg.No.KA 05MB0234 on 2622021 at about 3.50 p.m.
behind Anjaneyaswamy temple road, near temple cross, Bilidevalaya village, Kunigal Taluk, Tumakuru ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
5.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and in his support P.W.2 is examined.
Exs. P1
to P29
documents are marked.
The respondent No.2 got examined one Madhukumar D.N. MRO at Tumkur MM multispeciality hospital as RW1 and got marked ExR1 and R2.

B.K. Venkatesh Murthy vs Prakash.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51317535/
2 6.
Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

7. My answers to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following: JUDGMENT REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the car bearing reg.No.KA05MB0234, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 29 documents as ExP1 to 29 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, panchanama, charge sheet, IMV report, adhaar card, DL, pan card, discharge summary, medical prescriptions, medical bills, x rays, wound certificate and insurance policy.

9. The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Bettaswamy gowda S/o Rangegowda, the Kunigal police conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and filed ExP6 charge sheet against the driver of the car bearing reg.No.KA05MB0234 for the offenses punishable under Sec's.279, 338 of IPC, holding that accident in question has been taken place due to the the rash & negligent driving of car bearing reg.No.KA05 MB0234.
There is nothing on record to believe that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
JUDGMENT 10. On Perusal of the cross examination by the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Insurance company goes to show that the factum of accident is not denied by it.

Only suggestions were made to the effect that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and not due to the negligence of the riding of the car bearing reg.No.KA05MB0234 which were out rightly denied.
Under such circumstances oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence produced by the petitioner has to be accepted.
11. ExP5 wound certificate disclose that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
The respondent No.2 got examined one Madhukumar D.N.MRO at M.M hospital, Kunigal as RW1 and he produced ExR1 authorization letter and MLC register at ExR2.

Even ExR2 MLC extract clearly shows that the accident has been taken place on 2622021 and soon after the accident,
petitioner was admitted to the hospital.
mere delay in filing the complaint is not fatal and would not disentitle the petitioner JUDGMENT for compensation as petitioner being injured was took for treatment to the hospital.
Hence there is no reason to disbelieve the same.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, they have not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defense or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.
12. The respondent No.2 has disputed the involvement of the vehicle and the occurrence of the accident as there was a delay of 6 days in filing the complaint.

But on perusal of the cross examination of the PW1, respondent counsel has not disputed the occurrence of the accident,
involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.

Apart from this, on perusal of the documents,
ExP1 FIR, it is clearly stated that as the complainant was with the injured in the hospital, there was B.K. Venkatesh Murthy vs Prakash.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51317535/
3 a delay of six days in filing the complaint.

Even ExP4 and 5 vehicle seizure mahazar and ExP7 IMV report establishes the involvement of vehicle and ExP11discharge summary clearly shows that soon after the accident on 262 2021 petitioner was admitted to the hospital.
All these documents clearly shows that occurrence of the accident and JUDGMENT the involvement of the vehicle and all these documents are not at all disputed by the respondent.

13. With regard to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle, though respondent denied that the accident has not been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the car, but respondent has not made any suggestion with regard to the same and denied the evidence of the PW1 at least by way of putting any single suggestion.
15. Apart from this, as per ExP3 spot mahazar the accident has been taken place on the southern side of the road proceeding from Sriranganatha temple towards Kunigal.

Admittedly the offending vehicle was coming from western side i.e., Ranganatha swamy temple and proceeding towards Kunigal road and petitioner was proceeding from Kunigal towards Sriranganatha temple and the road was 12 feet width and accident had been taken place on the southern edge of the road within 2 feet from the southern edge.
Thus it clearly shows that the accident has been taken place as the offending car drove towards the wrong side of road.
Thus ExP3 clearly establishes that the accident has been taken JUDGMENT place due to the rash and negligent driving of the car.
14. Though the insurance company denied the cause of the accident as well as the very involvement of its insured vehicle, it has not let in any cogent evidence to this effect.
No doubt, the MRO at MM hospital, Kunigal got examined as RW.1, but his evidence is no way helpful to prove the defence of insurance company.
Because he is not an eyewitness to the accident and his evidence is not supported by any document or any independent witness.
Further, the insurance company did not make any attempt to examine the driver of car, who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non examination of driver of said vehicle is fatal to the defence of insurance company.
15. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of car bearing JUDGMENT reg.No.KA05MB0234.
16.

Even otherwise, it is a settled law that in a claim petition, the claimant need not prove the happening of events beyond reasonable doubt and the rule of preponderance of probability would apply in such cases.

In the decision reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819 (Bimla Devi & others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation & others), it has been held that in a Road accident, the strict principles of proof as in a Criminal case are not attracted.

entities.text: AIR 2009 SC 2819 (Bimla Devi & others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Relevant portion of the said decision is reproduced as follows:
" In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.

It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular Bus, in a particular manner, may not be possible to be done by the B.K. Venkatesh Murthy vs Prakash.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51317535/
4 claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of Proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
17. The point that merits consideration is that JUDGMENT the degree of proof required for proving the negligence on the part of the driver of car bearing reg.No.KA05MB0234.
In the present proceedings, is not as vigorous as is laid in proving the guilt of the accused in criminal trial.

The intent of the Motor Vehicles Act is benevolent and the entire purpose of the Legislation is likely to be defeated if in each case the petitioner is asked to prove the involvement and negligence on the part of the driver beyond reasonable doubt.

18. Therefore by applying the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in the decisions cited supra, to the facts of the instant proceedings, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident due to rash and negligent driving of car bearing reg.No.KA05MB0234 by its driver.
Hence issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of car bearing reg.No.KA JUDGMENT 05MB0234.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
20. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 40 years.
The petitioner has produced the Adhaar card as per Ex.P.8, it disclose the date of birth of the petitioner as 1021979 and the accident took place on 2622021.
So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 42 year.

The petitioner has stated that he was doing agriculture and earning more than Rs.5 lakhs p.a. and along with archak work and jyothisha shasthra telling he was earning Rs.1000/ per day and due to accidental injuries, he is suffering from permanent disability and deformity.
The petitioner has not produced any document to prove his avocation and income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.

In the absence of proof taking into consideration the date of accident, age of the petitioner and nature of her work, if his income is assessed at Rs.15,000/ JUDGMENT p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
21. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : i.e., (1) communited supra condylar fracture of left femur inter condylar extension.
The doctor has mentioned in the wound certificate that the said injury No.1 is grievous in nature.
It is needless to say that the said injury No.1 is grievous in nature.

Ex.P11 discharge summary discloses that for the aforesaid injuries, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Vijayanagar hospital from 2622021 to 132021 for total period of 4 days and underwent surgeries i.e., ORIF left distal femur with LCP and bone grafting under SA on 272 2021.

The petitioner further took treatment as inpatient at Vijayanagar hospital from 1372023 to 1572023 for total period of 3 days wherein diagnosed i.e., united fracture of left SC femur with implant insitu and it reveals from discharge summary that removal of implant left distal femur under SA on 1472023.

B.K. Venkatesh Murthy vs Prakash.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51317535/
5 22.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to JUDGMENT the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined Dr.Vinay as PW.2 who stated that at the time of examination, petitioner had pain left knee region, unable to walk and lacerated wound left knee region with bleeding and xray showed comminuted supra condylar fracture of left femur with inter condylar extension.

PW2 further stated that local examination shows cut lacerated over left knee 4 x 4 cm in size, 10 cm proximal to superior pole of patella,
underwent surgery ORIF left distal femur with LCP and bone grafting under spinal anesthesia on 2722021.

PW2 stated that petitioner is having disability in relation to the left lower limb at 80%
and for wholebody at 26.6%.
But however PW2 in his cross examination has admitted that the fracture has been united and the such type of injuries will be recovered within 3 to 6 months.
further PW2 clearly admitted that there is no problem to the petitioner for his movement.
23. From the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that JUDGMENT it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another.
24.

entities.text: Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner being Agriculturist, doing Archak work and jyotishya shastra can do work with some disability.
Hence, economical or functional disability to the extent of 15%, cannot be ruled out.
Therefore, I consider the functional disability of petitioner at 15%.
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of 41 to 45 age is '14'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.15,000/ p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.3,78,000/ JUDGMENT (Rs.15,000 X 12 X 14 X 15/100) is awarded under this head.

25. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :
As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the fractures and grievous injuries in the accident and he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and petitioner had sustained communited supra condylar fracture of left femur with inter condylar extension and he has taken the treatment as inpatient for two times totally for 7 days at Vijayanagar hospital and undergone two operations.

The petitioner has stated that he is suffering permanent disablement and deformity to attend his previous agriculture work and very difficult to climb hill i.e., Rangaswamy guddada for perform Archak work and wounds still paining and taking followup treatment due to permanent disablement and he has to undergo one more surgery.
Hence petitioner is suffering from with whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being 42 years and certainly JUDGMENT undergone severe pain and mental agony.

Looking into the nature of the wounds and B.K. Venkatesh Murthy vs Prakash.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51317535/
6 age of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/ under this head.
26. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAIDUP PERIOD: By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the hospital from 2622021 to 132021 as per ExP11 discharge summary and as per ExP27 discharge summary petitioner was admitted to the hospital from 1372022 to 15 72023 for removal of the implants.
thus petitioner was admitted in the hospital for total period of 7 days as inpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 5 months.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner it is quite natural that he could not have carried out his avocation for at least 4 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.75,000/ (15,000 X 5) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
JUDGMENT 27. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly as per the materials available on record, petitioner is residing in Kothagere hobli,
Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur and have treatment at M.M.Multispeciality hospital, Kunigal and Vijayanagar hospital, Bangalore as inpatient and certainly he would have hired the cab for traveling to the hospital.

entities.text: M.M.Multispeciality hospital, Kunigal and Vijayanagar hospital, Bangalore
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Admittedly, petitioner has taken the treatment as inpatient for two times for total period of 7 days and undergone 2 surgeries as per ExP11 and ExP27 and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/ under this head.
28. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face depression, anxiety, disappointment & frustration and also JUDGMENT suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.25,000/ is awarded under this head.
29. MEDICAL EXPENSES.
As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the document as per Ex.P.13 i.e.,medical bills for Rs.1,66,500/ and ExP12prescriptions.
ExP28medical prescriptions and ExP29 medical bills for Rs.1,07,730/.

The respondents have not disputed the said medical bills,
except denial suggestion.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.2,74,230/ under the head of medical expenses.

30. The calculation table stands as follows :
B.K. Venkatesh Murthy vs Prakash.N on 15 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51317535/
7

1 Attendant charges, extra : 25,00000 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain & sufferings : 50,00000 3 Loss of income during laid : 75,00000 up period 4 Loss of future income due : 3,78,00000 JUDGMENT to disability 5 Loss of future amenities & : 25,00000 happiness 6
Medical expenses : 2,74,23000 Total Rs.8,27,23000 31.
INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
32. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending car bearing reg.No.KA05MB0234 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly & severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in JUDGMENT the Affirmative'.
33. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.8,27,23000 with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.

After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
JUDGMENT Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to stenographer directly on computer, typed by her, corrected, signed and then pronounced by me in open court on this 15th day of April 2024).

(Chetana S.F.) IV Addl., Small Cause Judge & ACMM, Court of Small Causes,
BENGALURU.
